I need to decide whether to bid on Kentucky Avenue in the auction.

I'm in jail with $1179. The auction for Kentucky Avenue has a current high bid of $21. No player currently holds a complete red monopoly.

A bid of $1 would complete no red set. The hard cap is roughly $100. p4 has only $74 cash. I should drop out if pushed past that limit.

p4 owns Park Place and Boardwalk. p3 has $97 cash but still needs Indiana to complete the red set. The mortgage value of Kentucky is $110.

Owning Kentucky would block p3 from completing the red set if they ever acquire Indiana. p1 is nearly broke and would need to trade for that property. My cash is healthy enough to cover a bid. I will stay in the auction.

p3 bid $20 to pair with Illinois. p4 can afford the $21 bid without serious financial damage. Blocking p3 from completing reds is only partially useful because Indiana is mortgaged and p1 may not trade it. The base rent of $18 makes Kentucky a weak standalone income property.

I will bid the minimum $22 to stay in the auction. p3 could mortgage their four unmortgaged railroads for roughly $400, but they would need to sacrifice their main income engine to buy a non-monopoly property.

The green monopoly is the priority. I need Pennsylvania Avenue from the bank, and cash must survive upcoming orange and pink hits. I have enough cushion to bid $22 for Kentucky.

I will bid $22 to stay in the auction. I do not want to reveal my ceiling, but I will drop if the price rises above roughly $80 or $100. p4 is the current leader at $21, so I need to watch for a response from them or p3.

Dropping out would not guarantee p4 wins; p3 likely bids $22 or higher. I will stay in to either win cheaply or force p3 to overpay. p3 has $97 cash, so pushing them toward $70–90 would drain their liquidity. Their pink properties are already built and generating rent, so this hurts their ability to pay upcoming orange and pink hits.

I have served two jail turns. The next turn I must roll doubles or pay $50 to exit. Turn 92 is p1's auction turn, not mine.
